prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Provided is an exhibition device that is installed in a store, for example, and controls the display mode of a product image so as to call the attention of a user to a product and also arouse the interest of the user. The exhibition device is provided with an exhibition region in which an object (such as a product) is exhibited and a display region of an image corresponding to the object, and changes the display mode of the display region on the basis of object information relating to the object and/or moving body information relating to a moving body (such as a user). In addition, an exhibition system is composed of the exhibition device and an information processing device that estimates whether the moving body is interested in the object exhibited in the exhibition region. Due to this configuration, the exhibition device is able to change the display mode of the display region corresponding to an image of an object in which a moving body is estimated to be interested.

The exhibition device includes an exhibition region in which an object, such as a product, is exhibited, and a display region for displaying an image corresponding to the object. The exhibition device changes the display mode of the display region on the basis of object information relating to the object and/or moving body information relating to a moving body, such as a user. In addition, an exhibition system is configured from the exhibition device and an information processing device that estimates whether the moving body is interested in the object exhibited in the exhibition region. With this configuration, the exhibition device can change the display mode of the display region corresponding to an image of an object in which the moving body is estimated to be interested.
outputs.L2:
An exhibition device is disclosed that may be placed in a retail store or similar location and that adjusts how a product image is shown in order to draw a user’s attention to the product and increase the user’s interest. The device includes an exhibition area where an item, such as a product, is displayed, together with a display area for presenting an image associated with that item. The manner in which the display area presents the image is modified based on information about the item and/or information about a moving body, such as a user.

An exhibition system is also provided. This system includes the exhibition device and an information processing device that determines whether the moving body is interested in the item shown in the exhibition area. With this arrangement, the exhibition device can alter the display style of the display area for an image corresponding to an item in which the moving body is estimated to have interest.
outputs.L3:
The exhibition device is intended to be installed in a store, showroom, exhibition hall, or other similar location where products or objects are presented to users. By presenting the object together with related visual information, the device attracts the attention of users passing nearby and encourages them to develop interest in the exhibited product.

The device includes an exhibition region and a display region. The exhibition region is configured to physically display an object, such as a product, sample, model, or other item to be promoted. The display region is configured to show an image corresponding to the object displayed in the exhibition region. For example, the display region may present a product image, explanatory video, advertising content, usage scene, specification information, or other visual content associated with the exhibited object.

The display mode of the display region may be changed dynamically. This change may be performed based on information relating to the exhibited object, information relating to a moving body such as a user near the device, or a combination of both. The information relating to the object may include the type, category, position, state, or identification information of the object. The information relating to the moving body may include the user’s position, movement direction, distance from the device, line of sight, stopping behavior, gesture, or other behavior indicating attention or interest. Based on such information, the device may change the size, brightness, color, animation, content, layout, or timing of the image displayed in the display region.

An exhibition system may include the exhibition device and an information processing device. The information processing device is configured to acquire or receive information about the moving body and estimate whether the user is interested in the exhibited object. For instance, the information processing device may determine that the user is interested when the user approaches the exhibition device, stops in front of the object, looks toward the object or the display region, or remains near the object for a predetermined period of time.

When it is estimated that a moving body, such as a user, is interested in a particular exhibited object, the exhibition device may modify the display mode of an image corresponding to that object. For example, the device may enlarge the image, increase its brightness, switch to a more detailed explanation, play a promotional video, highlight key features, or display related product information. In this way, the exhibition device can provide a more effective presentation tailored to the user’s behavior and interest, thereby improving the appeal of the exhibited object and increasing the likelihood of user engagement.
outputs.L4:
An exhibition device and system for use in stores, showrooms, museums, and similar display spaces presents product images in association with physical objects that are being exhibited. The system includes one or more display units arranged near the exhibited objects, such as merchandise, samples, models, or promotional items. Each display unit can show images, videos, descriptions, advertisements, pricing information, usage scenes, comparison information, or other content related to the corresponding object. By visually linking the digital content with the physical object, the system helps users understand the object more easily and encourages them to pay attention to products that may otherwise be overlooked.

The system changes the manner in which product images are displayed based on information relating to the exhibited object and/or information relating to a moving body, such as a customer or visitor near the exhibit. Object information may include the type, position, category, stock status, sales priority, popularity, or identification information of the exhibited object. Moving-body information may include the presence, position, movement direction, walking speed, viewing distance, stopping time, line of sight, posture, gesture, or behavior of a user. This information may be obtained using sensors, cameras, RFID readers, beacons, depth sensors, motion detectors, touch panels, or other detection devices installed in or near the exhibition area.

When a user approaches an exhibited object, the system can determine whether the user is likely to be interested in that object. For example, if the user slows down, stops in front of the object, looks at it for a certain period of time, reaches toward it, picks it up, or repeatedly returns to the same display area, the system may estimate that the user has a relatively high level of interest. Conversely, if the user merely passes by without slowing down or looking at the object, the system may determine that the level of interest is low. The estimation may be performed by analyzing the acquired object information and moving-body information according to predetermined rules or by using a trained model.

Based on the estimated level of interest, the system changes the display mode of the image or other content associated with the exhibited object. The display mode may include the size, brightness, color, layout, animation, timing, order, amount of information, or type of content shown on the display. For a user who appears to have low interest, the system may present a more eye-catching image, a short promotional video, a highlighted feature, or a special offer in order to attract attention. For a user who appears to have high interest, the system may provide more detailed product information, usage examples, specifications, reviews, related products, or purchase guidance. In this way, the system can provide content that is appropriate to the user’s behavior and level of engagement.

The exhibition device may also coordinate multiple displays. For instance, when a user moves from one object to another, the system may change the content on nearby displays so that the user can easily compare products or follow a guided presentation. If several users are present, the system may select content based on the user closest to a particular object, the user showing the strongest interest, or the overall flow of people in the exhibition area. The system may also record interaction data, such as which objects attract attention, how long users view them, and which display modes are most effective. This data can be used by store operators to improve product placement, promotional strategies, and future display content.

By combining physical exhibition with adaptive digital presentation, the device and system make product displays more responsive and engaging. The system can automatically change image display modes according to the situation around the exhibited object, rather than presenting the same fixed content to every user. As a result, it becomes possible to attract users’ attention more effectively, increase the time they spend interacting with products, support purchasing decisions, and improve the overall effectiveness of store exhibitions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following patent abstract in plain English: an exhibition device installed in a store with an exhibition region for a product and a display region for an image, where the display changes based on object information and user movement/interest estimation.
counterfactuals.output: A store display setup shows a product in one area and related images or information on a screen in another area. It detects details about the product or nearby objects and tracks how shoppers move or show interest. Based on that information, it automatically changes what appears on the display to better match the shopper’s attention or behavior.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of an invention involving a store exhibition device that displays product images and changes the display mode according to information about the exhibited object and a nearby moving body such as a customer.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a store exhibition device for presenting products using an image display unit. The device acquires object information about an exhibited product and moving-body information about a nearby person, such as a customer, through sensors or other detection means. Based on these inputs, a control unit determines an appropriate display mode and changes how product images are shown.

For example, the device may display standard product images when no customer is nearby, switch to an attention-attracting mode when a customer approaches, and present detailed or customized product information according to the customer’s position, movement, or interaction with the exhibited object. By dynamically controlling the image display mode in accordance with both the displayed product and the behavior or presence of a moving body, the device improves product presentation effectiveness and customer engagement in a retail environment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style abstract for an exhibition system comprising an exhibition device and an information processing device, where the system estimates whether a user is interested in a displayed product and modifies the corresponding image display mode.
counterfactuals.output: An exhibition system includes an exhibition device configured to display a product and an information processing device communicably connected to the exhibition device. The information processing device acquires user information relating to a user viewing the product, estimates, based on the acquired user information, whether the user is interested in the product, and controls an image display mode corresponding to the product in accordance with a result of the estimation. The exhibition device displays an image associated with the product in the controlled image display mode, thereby enabling presentation of product information to be dynamically changed according to an estimated interest state of the user.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an exhibition device that attracts user attention to products by controlling a product-image display area based on product information and customer movement information, including an associated system for estimating user interest.
counterfactuals.output:
An exhibition device can be configured to draw a customer’s attention to displayed products by dynamically controlling a product-image display area according to both product information and customer movement information.

The device includes:

- **A product display unit** that physically exhibits one or more products.
- **A product-image display area**, such as a screen, projection area, transparent display, or lighting/display panel positioned near the exhibited products.
- **A product information acquisition unit** that stores or receives product information, for example product type, name, price, features, promotion status, stock status, recommended use, or priority level.
- **A customer movement detection unit** that detects movement information of a customer near the exhibition device. This may include position, walking direction, distance from the product, speed, stopping time, gaze direction, body orientation, or approach/leave behavior, using cameras, depth sensors, infrared sensors, beacons, pressure sensors, or other detection means.
- **A control unit** that determines how to control the product-image display area based on the product information and the detected customer movement information.
- **A display control unit** that changes the display content, size, position, brightness, animation, timing, or emphasis of product images in the product-image display area.

For example, when a customer approaches a particular product, the device may enlarge or highlight an image of that product, display related information, show an animation, or move the image toward the customer’s viewing direction. If the customer slows down or stops, the device may present more detailed product information. If the customer passes by quickly, the device may display a short attention-attracting image or promotional message.

The associated system for estimating user interest includes:

- **A behavior information collection unit** that collects customer movement data around the exhibition device.
- **An interaction analysis unit** that analyzes behaviors such as approach frequency, dwell time, repeated viewing, distance from the product, head or gaze direction, hand movement, and response to displayed images.
- **An interest estimation unit** that estimates a degree of customer interest in each product based on the analyzed behavior.
- **A feedback/control unit** that feeds the estimated interest level back to the exhibition device so that the product-image display area can be further controlled.

The interest estimation system may determine, for instance, that a customer has high interest when the customer approaches slowly, stops in front of the product, looks toward the product-image display area, or repeatedly returns to the product. Conversely, low interest may be estimated when the customer walks past without slowing down or faces away from the product.

Based on the estimated interest, the exhibition device may adaptively change the display, such as:

- emphasizing the product that appears to interest the customer most;
- displaying more detailed specifications or use examples;
- showing comparison information with related products;
- presenting a coupon or promotional message;
- changing the display timing or visual effects to regain attention.

In this way, the exhibition device actively attracts user attention by coordinating product-image presentation with real-time customer movement and estimated customer interest, thereby improving product appeal and supporting more effective product promotion.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert this invention concept into a formal patent abstract: a retail display apparatus has an exhibition area for objects and an image display area, and changes the display appearance when an information processor determines that a moving person is interested in the exhibited object.
counterfactuals.output: A retail display apparatus includes an exhibition area configured to display an object and an image display area configured to display visual information associated with the object. An information processor detects a moving person in the vicinity of the apparatus and determines whether the moving person has an interest in the exhibited object based on behavior or position information of the moving person. When the information processor determines that the moving person is interested in the exhibited object, the apparatus changes a display appearance of at least one of the exhibition area and the image display area, thereby presenting information or visual effects adapted to the detected interest of the person.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
